title: Post title hardcodes the 2% cap instead of deriving it from rpz
evidence: rent_post.gleam (Q2 post): '  title: "Dublin Rents Q2 2026: What Landlords Can Actually Charge Under the 2% Cap",' — rpz.gleam: 'pub const cap_ceiling_bps: Int = 200' and '  annual_rate_bps: 340,' — rent_post.gleam type doc (pre-existing): '/// Full SEO title and H1. The body derives its cap figures from `rpz`; the /// title itself carries the issue-mandated "2% Cap" phrase verbatim.' — rpz.gleam doc: 'The legal cap is the LOWER of this and the 2% statutory ceiling, so we store CPI to stay correct if it ever dips below 2%.'
detail: Acceptance says "No hardcoded cap percentage in copy (derives from rpz)". Body copy derives correctly, and 2% equals today's binding cap (min(340,200)bps), matching the Q1 precedent — but the title is a literal that goes stale the moment CPI dips below 2%, a case rpz explicitly anticipates.
recommended_fix: Either derive the title's cap phrase at render time like binding_cap_clause(), or add a guard to the cpi-bump workflow that flags/retires the series titles when CPI drops below cap_ceiling_bps.
